react_result.final_narrative_text: Seven metabolites significantly altered between control and treatment groups resolve into two distinct biological themes. The dominant signal is a profound perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, observed with extraordinary consistency across three independent analytical paradigms: multi-database ORA (RaMP, FDR 2.9×10⁻¹⁵), KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment (MetaboAnalystR, p=2.5×10⁻⁶), and m/z-direct network analysis (Mummichog, p=8.4×10⁻⁵). Five androgen and estrogen intermediates drove this signal — dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estrone, and 17β-estradiol — all captured in the androgen-and-estrogen metabolism module (KEGG:map00150) and its SMPDB counterpart (SMPDB:SMP00068), which also encompasses the Reactome Metabolism of steroid hormones pathway (REACT:R-HSA-196071) and the estrogen-biosynthesis sub-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-193144). The 100% overlap between the input steroid set and the top Mummichog C21-steroid hormone pathway and the near-maximal fold-enrichment in ORA (≈1668×) indicate that the treatment condition drives a wholesale shift in the circulating steroid pool, consistent with either aromatase inhibition, 17β-HSD dysregulation, or androgen-receptor pathway activation. The secondary signal originates from N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074), which Mummichog maps to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (KEGG:C00140) via identical block-14 InChIKey, reflecting a stereoisomer relationship (galacto/gluco) confirmed by reconcile_inchikey. This amino-sugar engages hyaluronan metabolism, sialic acid metabolism, and N-glycan degradation (all rank 2–4 in Mummichog), consistent with altered glycosaminoglycan processing. Guanidoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581) independently engages the urea cycle/amino-group metabolism and glycine/serine/alanine/threonine nodes. The convergent multi-paradigm evidence points to steroid hormone pathway disruption as the primary biological consequence of the treatment, with secondary perturbations in amino-sugar and guanidino metabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm pathway analysis of seven differentially abundant metabolites reveals a dominant perturbation in androgen and estrogen metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR 2.93×10⁻¹⁵ and fold-enrichment 1668×, with five steroid intermediates (estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one) out of 27 pathway members. This finding is independently corroborated by MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (hsa00140, p=2.51×10⁻⁶) and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.40×10⁻⁵), where all 11 input steroid compounds map to the pathway with 100% overlap. The five driver steroids converge on C19/C18 steroid interconversion reactions (androstenedione, testosterone, DHEA, estrone, and estradiol) within the canonical sex-steroid biosynthesis axis. Guanidoacetic acid appears in secondary Mummichog hits for glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism (rank 5) and urea cycle/amino group metabolism (rank 6), both at p=0.056. N-acetylgalactosamine maps to N-glycan degradation and hyaluronan metabolism via mass-based annotation, consistent with its distinct biochemical class. The three-method consensus confirms steroid hormone pathway disruption as the primary biological signal.

This finding is independently corroborated by MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (hsa00140, p=2.51×10⁻⁶) and Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p=8.40×10⁻⁵), where all 11 input steroid compounds map to the pathway with 100% overlap. The five driver steroids converge on C19/C18 steroid interconversion reactions (androstenedione, testosterone, DHEA, estrone, and estradiol) within the canonical sex-steroid biosynthesis axis. Guanidoacetic acid appears in secondary Mummichog hits for glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism (rank 5) and urea cycle/amino group metabolism (rank 6), both at p=0.056. N-acetylgalactosamine maps to N-glycan degradation and hyaluronan metabolism via mass-based annotation, consistent with its distinct biochemical class. The three-method consensus confirms steroid hormone pathway disruption as the primary biological signal.
